content: 1. A study published in the Journal of Clinical Tuberculosis and Other Mycobacterial Diseases in 2017 (Volume 7, Pages 22–27) examined the risk of tuberculosis (TB) among contacts of patients with isoniazid-resistant and isoniazid-susceptible TB. This research highlights the importance of understanding drug resistance in TB transmission dynamics. 2. Radhakrishnan et al. (2011) investigated the risk of TB among contacts of isoniazid-resistant and isoniazid-susceptible cases in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 15, Issue 6, Pages 782–788). Their findings emphasize the need for tailored interventions based on drug resistance profiles. 3. Rakotosamimanana et al. (2015) conducted a prospective cohort study to identify biomarkers for predicting the risk of developing active TB among contacts of TB patients. Published in the European Respiratory Journal (Volume 46, Issue 4, Pages 1095–1103), this study underscores the potential of biomarkers in early TB detection. 4. Ramos et al. (2013) evaluated TB screening among family and household contacts in rural Ethiopia over a 20-month period. Their findings, published in the International Journal of Mycobacteriology (Volume 2, Issue 4, Pages 240–243), highlight the challenges and outcomes of community-based TB screening programs. 5. Ranganath and Hamsa (2018) analyzed child contact screening and chemoprophylaxis against TB in South Indian districts. Their study, published in the Indian Journal of Public Health Research and Development (Volume 9, Issue 3, Pages 341–344), provides insights into the implementation of preventive strategies for pediatric TB. 6. Rizwan et al. (2013) explored TB screening among household contacts of index patients in Pakistan. Published in the Pakistan Journal of Medical Research (Volume 52, Issue 4, Pages 96–101), this study highlights the importance of contact tracing in TB control. 7. Rutherford et al. (2012) identified risk factors for Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection in Indonesian children living with sputum smear-positive cases. Their findings, published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 16, Issue 12, Pages 1594–1599), emphasize the vulnerability of children in high-risk households. 8. Rutherford et al. (2012) compared the QuantiFERON-TB Gold In-Tube assay with the tuberculin skin test in Indonesian children exposed to TB. Published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 16, Issue 4, Pages 496–502), this study evaluates diagnostic tools for latent TB infection. 9. Said et al. (2019) investigated immunologic-based diagnosis of latent TB among children under five years of age in Tanzania. Their study, published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal (Volume 38, Issue 4, Pages 333–339), highlights the challenges of diagnosing latent TB in young children. 10. Sanai et al. (2016) evaluated passive and active approaches to improve TB notifications in Afghanistan. Published in PLOS One (Volume 11, Issue 10, e0163813), this study provides evidence for enhancing TB case detection through active case-finding strategies. 11. Sasilia et al. (2016) examined the relationship between household contact with TB patients and associated risk factors in East Aceh Regency. This study emphasizes the importance of understanding household-level risk factors in TB transmission. 12. Saunders et al. (2017) developed a scoring system to predict and stratify TB risk among adult contacts of index cases. Published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases (Volume 17, Issue 11, Pages 1190–1199), this study offers a tool for targeted TB prevention. 13. Saunders et al. (2019) conducted a 10-year prospective cohort study on active and passive case-finding in TB-affected households in Peru. Published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases (Volume 19, Issue 5, Pages 519–528), this research highlights the long-term impact of active case-finding. 14. Seddon et al. (2013) investigated preventive therapy for child contacts of multidrug-resistant TB in a prospective cohort study. 15. Seddon et al. (2013) also conducted a cross-sectional study to identify risk factors for infection and disease in child contacts of multidrug-resistant TB. Published in BMC Infectious Diseases (Volume 13, Article 392), this study provides insights into the epidemiology of pediatric TB. 16. Shah et al. (2013) implemented an integrated approach to active contact investigation and treatment support in rural and urban Sindh, Pakistan. Published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 17, Issue 12, Pages 1569–1574), this study highlights the benefits of integrated TB care. 17. Shapiro et al. (2012) evaluated community-based targeted case-finding for TB and HIV among household contacts in South Africa. Published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine (Volume 185, Issue 10, Pages 1110–1116), this study demonstrates the effectiveness of community-based interventions. 18. Sharma et al. (2017) compared the tuberculin skin test (TST) and interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) for diagnosing latent TB infection in high-burden settings. Published in PLOS One (Volume 12, Issue 1, e0169539), this study evaluates diagnostic accuracy in resource-limited settings. 19. Shivaramakrishna et al. (2014) assessed isoniazid preventive treatment in children in South India, examining whether practice aligns with policy. Published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 18, Issue 8, Pages 919–924), this study highlights gaps in policy implementation. 20. Sinfield et al. (2006) identified risk factors for TB infection and disease in young childhood contacts in Malawi. Published in Annals of Tropical Paediatrics (Volume 26, Issue 3, Pages 205–213), this study emphasizes the need for targeted interventions in high-burden areas. 21. Singh et al. (2013) investigated the incidence and prevalence of TB among household contacts of pulmonary TB patients in peri-urban South Delhi, India. Published in PLOS One (Volume 8, Issue 7, e69730), this study highlights the burden of TB in urban settings. 22. Singh et al. (2017) evaluated the effectiveness of isoniazid preventive therapy among children living with TB patients in Bhopal, India. Published in Journal of Tropical Pediatrics (Volume 63, Issue 4, Pages 274–285), this study underscores the importance of preventive therapy in pediatric TB control. 23. Single et al. (2011) examined TB among household contacts of multidrug-resistant TB patients in Delhi, India. Published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 15, Issue 10, Pages 1326–1330), this study highlights the challenges of managing drug-resistant TB. 24. Szkwarcko et al. (2018) implemented a clinic-based child TB contact management strategy in western Kenya. Published in Public Health Action (Volume 8, Issue 2, Pages 91–94), this study demonstrates the feasibility of clinic-based interventions. 25. Tadesse et al. (2016) evaluated the uptake of isoniazid preventive therapy among under-five children in Ethiopia. Published in PLOS One (Volume 11, Issue 5, e0155525), this study highlights the role of contact investigation as an entry point for preventive therapy. 26. Tefara et al. (2019) assessed facilityand community-based active household TB contact investigation in Ethiopia. Published in BMC Health Services Research (Volume 19, Article 234), this study provides evidence for community-based TB interventions. 27. Thanh et al. (2014) conducted a household survey on TB screening practices among contacts of smear-positive TB patients in Vietnam. Published in BMC Public Health (Volume 14), this study highlights gaps in TB screening practices. 28. Thind et al. (2012) evaluated a household TB contact tracing program in South Africa. Published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 16, Issue 12, Pages 1643–1648), this study demonstrates the effectiveness of contact tracing in high-burden settings. 29. Tieu et al. (2014) compared interferon-gamma release assays with the tuberculin skin test in Thai children exposed to TB. Published in PLOS One (Volume 9, Issue 8, e105003), this study evaluates diagnostic tools for pediatric TB. 30. Titiyos et al. (2015) assessed the yield of screening symptomatic contacts of multidrug-resistant TB cases in Ethiopia. Published in BMC Research Notes (Volume 8, Article 501), this study highlights the importance of targeted screening. 31. Togun et al. (2015) evaluated the contribution of Xpert MTB/RIF to diagnosing pulmonary TB among TB-exposed children in The Gambia. Published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 19, Issue 9, Pages 1091–1097), this study underscores the utility of molecular diagnostics. 32. Triasih et al. (2015) evaluated chest X-ray use in community-based screening of child TB contacts in Indonesia. Published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 19, Issue 12, Pages 1428–1434), this study highlights the role of radiography in TB screening. 33. Van Kampen et al. (2015) assessed the impact of introducing Xpert MTB/RIF for testing and treating individuals at risk of multidrug-resistant TB in Kazakhstan. Published in PLOS One (Volume 10, Issue 7, e0132514), this study demonstrates the benefits of rapid molecular diagnostics. 34. Vella et al. (2011) investigated household contact tracing of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant TB in high HIV prevalence settings. Published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 15, Issue 9, Pages 1170–1175), this study highlights the challenges of managing TB in co-endemic regions. 35. Whalen et al. (2011) examined the secondary attack rate of TB in urban households in Kampala, Uganda. Published in PLOS One (Volume 6, Issue 2, e16137), this study provides insights into TB transmission dynamics in urban settings. 36. Wysocki et al. (2016) evaluated the latent TB infection diagnostic and treatment cascade among contacts in primary healthcare in São Paulo, Brazil. Published in PLOS One (Volume 11, Issue 6, e0155348), this study highlights gaps in the TB care cascade. 37. Yuen et al. (2019) assessed household accompaniment to improve TB contact management in Peru. Published in PLOS One (Volume 14, Issue 5), this study demonstrates the benefits of supportive interventions in TB care. 38. Van Schalkwyk et al. (2014) investigated the incidence of TB and HIV among household contacts of TB index patients in South Africa. Published in PLOS One (Volume 9, Issue 4, e95372), this study highlights the dual burden of TB and HIV in high-risk populations. 39. Salazar-Austin et al. (2019) conducted a cluster-randomized trial comparing symptom-based versus tuberculin skin test-based screening of household TB contacts under five years of age. Published in Clinical Infectious Diseases, this study evaluates strategies to improve TB preventive therapy uptake. 40. Page-Shipp et al. (2018) implemented household point-of-care CD4 testing and isoniazid preventive therapy initiation in South Africa. Published in PLOS One (Volume 13, Issue 3, e0192089), this study highlights the integration of TB and HIV care. 41. Hanrahan et al. (2019) compared contact tracing with facility-based screening for active TB case finding in rural South Africa. Published in PLOS Medicine (Volume 16, Issue 4, e1002796), this study evaluates the effectiveness of different case-finding approaches.
